header.title: Commedia III: Paradiso: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Dante Alighieri
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:dante:commedia:paradiso:petrocchi, from UD Italian-Old: Petrocchi's text via DanteSearch (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.7.147: 8.12 ‘or da coppa or da ciglio’: the sun is now behind Venus (‘coppa’, the nape), now before her (‘ciglio’, the brow), as evening and morning star.
notes.4.41: In this copy ‘però che’, which in Petrocchi opens 4.41 and 4.51, stands at the end of the line before (4.40, 4.50); the English follows the lines as given. 4.48 ‘Tobia’ is Tobit, the elder Tobias, healed of blindness.
notes.1.11: In this copy ‘Infino a’, which in Petrocchi opens 1.16, stands at the end of 1.15; the English follows the lines as given.
notes.28.14: 28.14 ‘volume’: the revolving sphere, here the Primum Mobile; rendered ‘rolling sphere’.
notes.29.35: In this copy ‘anzi che’ and ‘secondo che’, which in Petrocchi open 29.39 and 29.66, stand at the end of 29.38 and 29.65; the English follows the lines as given. 29.36 ‘vime … divima’: a withy (pliant twig used as a tie) that is never untwisted. 29.51 ‘il suggetto d’i vostri alimenti’: the lowest of the elements, earth, as the substrate of the rest.
notes.30.147: In this copy several words that in Petrocchi open the next line stand at the end of the line before: ‘là dove’ (before 30.147, 31.9, 31.12), ‘sì come’ (31.7), ‘sì che’ (31.24); the English follows the lines as given. 30.148 ‘Alagna’ is Anagni.
notes.33.92: 33.94–96: the sense of ‘letargo’ (forgetfulness) and of the comparison is much debated; read here as: one instant has made me forget more than twenty-five centuries have made the world forget the Argonauts’ voyage.

nodes.text: I could store up as treasure in my mind
shall now be the matter of my song.
O good Apollo, for the last labor
make me such a vessel of your power
as you require for giving the beloved laurel. Up to
this point one peak of Parnassus
was enough for me; but now with both
only from what the senses perceive does it grasp
what it then makes worthy of the intellect.
For this reason Scripture condescends
to your capacity, and feet and hands
it attributes to God, and means something else;
and Holy Church, with a human aspect,
shows Gabriel and Michael to you,
and the other who made Tobit sound again.
What Timaeus argues about souls
is not like what is seen here, since,
as he says it, so he seems to think it.
He says that the soul returns to its star,
believing it to have been cut off from there
when nature gave it as a form;
and perhaps his meaning is otherwise
than his words sound, and it may be
of an intent not to be mocked.
If he means that to these wheels return
the honor of their influence and the blame, perhaps
his bow strikes upon some truth.
This principle, ill understood, once twisted
almost the whole world, so that Jupiter,
Mercury and Mars it strayed so far as to name.
The other doubt that troubles you
has less poison, because its malice
how human flesh was made then,
when the first parents were both made.”
The world used to believe, to its peril,
that the fair Cyprian sent mad love
raying down, turning in the third epicycle;
so that not only to her did they do honor
with sacrifice and with votive cry,
the ancient peoples in the ancient error;
but they honored Dione and Cupid,
the one as her mother, the other as her son,
and they said that he sat in Dido’s lap;
and from her with whom I take my beginning
they took the name of the star
that the sun courts now at her nape, now at her brow.
I was not aware of rising into it;
but that I was within it I was made fully sure by
I saw another move, wheeling,
and gladness was the whip to the top.
So for Charlemagne and for Roland
my attentive gaze followed two of them,
as the eye follows its falcon in flight.
Next William and Renouard
and Duke Godfrey drew my sight
your finger into the fire, in the time I saw the sign
that follows Taurus, and was inside it.
O glorious stars, O light pregnant
with great power, from which I acknowledge
all of my talent, whatever it may be,
with you was rising and with you was setting
he who is father of every mortal life,
when I first felt the Tuscan air;
and then, when grace was granted me
to enter the high wheel that turns you,
your region was allotted me.
To you devoutly now there sighs
my soul, to acquire power
mine, by what appears in that rolling sphere
whenever one looks well into its circling,
I saw a point that rayed out light
so sharp that the sight it sets ablaze
must close because of its great keenness;
and downward so prevail that toward God
all are drawn and all draw.
And Dionysius with such longing
set himself to contemplate these orders
that he named and distinguished them as I do.
But Gregory afterwards parted from him;
so that, as soon as he opened his eyes
in this heaven, he laughed at himself.
And if so secret a truth was set forth
by a mortal on earth, I do not want you to marvel:
in the middle, potency was bound to act
by such a tie that it is never untied.
Jerome wrote to you of a long stretch
of ages, with the angels created before
the rest of the world was made;
but this truth is written in many places
by the writers of the Holy Spirit,
and you will perceive it if you look carefully;
and reason too sees it in some degree,
for it would not grant that the movers
were so long without their perfection.
Now you know where and when these loves
were created, and how: so that quenched
in your desire are already three flames.
Nor would one reach twenty, counting,
as quickly as a part of the angels
disturbed the substrate of your elements.
The other part remained, and began this art
which you discern, with such delight
that it never leaves off circling.
The beginning of the fall was the accursed
pride of the one you saw
pressed down by all the weights of the world.
Those you see here were modest
in acknowledging themselves as from the goodness
that had made them ready for such understanding:
for which their sight was exalted
by illuminating grace and by their merit,
so that they have a firm and full will;
and I do not want you to doubt, but to be certain
that to receive grace is meritorious in the measure that
Simon Magus is, for his deserts,
and will make the one from Anagni go further down.”
In the form, then, of a white rose
the holy army showed itself to me
that Christ in his own blood made his bride;
but the other, which, flying, sees and sings
the glory of him who fills it with love
and the goodness that made it so great, just as
a swarm of bees that plunges into the flowers
at one moment, and at another returns there where
its labor is turned to sweetness,
was descending into the great flower that is adorned
with so many petals, and from there rose again there where
its love forever dwells.
Their faces all were of living flame
and their wings of gold, and the rest so white
that no snow comes up to that degree.
When they descended into the flower, from tier to tier
they offered some of the peace and the ardor
which they gained as they fanned their sides.
Nor did the interposing, between what was above and the flower,
of so great a flying multitude
obstruct the sight or the splendor:
for the divine light penetrates
through the universe according as it is worthy, so that
nothing can stand in its way.
This secure and joyful kingdom,
thronged with people of old and with new,
I believe I saw, because, more amply,
as I say this, I feel that I rejoice.
A single instant is a greater oblivion to me
than twenty-five centuries to the enterprise
that made Neptune marvel at the shadow of the Argo.
So my mind, wholly suspended,
was gazing, fixed, motionless and intent,
